samples.summary: New `useDocumentsPath` hook issues an unconditional authenticated `fetchWorkspaces` with no `enabled`/`retry` gate, so any future mount on an anonymous share route would force a logout + hard redirect to /login
samples.evidence: `useDocumentsPath` (use-documents-path.ts:14-17) calls `useQuery({queryKey:["workspaces"], queryFn: fetchWorkspaces})` with no `enabled` condition and default retry. `fetchWorkspaces` goes through `fetchWithAuth` (api/workspaces.ts:40), and `fetchWithAuth` on a 401 that cannot be refreshed calls `logout(...)` and `redirectTo("/login")` before throwing `AuthExpiredError` (api/auth.ts:146-161). Today the hook is only mounted from `file-shell.tsx:62` and `file-detail.tsx:128`, both behind the authenticated `/f/:id` route, so it is not currently exploitable. But `ImageViewer` is deliberately mounted a second time by the anonymous share path (`app/shared/shared-document.tsx:766`) and that mount already has to defend against exactly this hazard — `image-viewer.tsx:95-116` disables its `document`/`documents` queries with `enabled: !token` precisely because "a request that 401s ... forces a login redirect". The hook carries no equivalent guard and no comment marking it authenticated-only, while the change's own notes advertise extending the `leading`/back affordance to other layouts as "a one-liner" (docs/tasks/active/20260822-image-viewer-back-button-lessons.md). An anonymous share-link visitor reaching this hook would be logged out of any unrelated session in that browser and bounced to /login, i.e. a session-handling denial rather than data exposure. Recommend an `enabled: <authenticated>` (or `token`-aware) gate plus `retry: false`, mirroring `ImageViewer`.
searchedFor: Grep 'ImageViewer|useDocumentsPath' across packages/frontend/src to enumerate every call site of the hook and the viewer
Grep 'FileShell|SiteHeader' across packages/frontend/src to confirm FileShell is not reachable from the public /shared route

samples.summary: Global capture-phase window keydown listener is now installed for the anonymous share-link mount too; harmless today but it is an app-wide key hook whose only gate is a DOM-attribute query
samples.evidence: `window.addEventListener("keydown", onKey, true)` (image-viewer.tsx:163) runs for every keystroke anywhere in the page, including on the anonymous share route where `ImageViewer` is mounted with a `token` (app/shared/shared-document.tsx:766). The handler reads only `e.key`/`e.target.tagName` and never logs, stores, or transmits anything, and with `onClose` undefined and prev/next queries disabled it is inert for the anonymous mount, so there is no data-exposure or navigation vector I could complete. Flagged only because the suppression decision rests entirely on `document.querySelector(OPEN_OVERLAY_SELECTOR)` (image-viewer.tsx:40-42) — a global, attribute-based DOM probe rather than React state — which is a fragile place to hang behaviour; no security impact identified.
